message.content:
**Decision: Buy AAPL — order filled.**

**What the 10-K showed (FY ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024):**
- Total net sales: $391,035M (up 2% from $383,285M)
- Gross margin: $180,683M (46.2% of sales, up from 44.1%)
- **Operating income: $123,216M** (up 8% from $114,301M) — the figure the task asked me to cite
- Net income: $93,736M; diluted EPS: $6.08 (net income was depressed by a one-time $10.2B net tax charge tied to the EC State Aid Decision, which did *not* touch operating income)
- Cash generated by operating activities: $118,254M; cash + marketable securities of $140.8B

**Order:** Buy 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.80 (quote: last $222.70, bid $222.68 / ask $222.72 — limit set at the ask, i.e., at market). Notional ≈ $9,803, under the $10,000 per-order cap and well within the $20,000 daily cap; this is the only order placed today, so total spend is ~$9,803. Buy-only, AAPL-only, funded from the $50,000 cash balance — no money moved out of the account.

**Why:** Apple's FY2024 filing shows a business that grew revenue modestly while expanding gross margin by 210 bps and lifting operating income 8% to $123.2B, with $118.3B of operating cash flow and a $110B buyback authorization — a high-quality, cash-generative franchise trading at a reasonable multiple. The headline net income decline is a tax/legal one-off (State Aid Decision), not an operating deterioration, so the operating-income trend is the better read on the business. I sized the position at just under the $10,000 per-order limit and used a market-level limit price to stay inside the mandate.
